selector.rationale: Soap-bubble appearance and cortical destruction on CT, along with avid enhancement on MRI, support Giant Cell Tumor diagnosis

rejected.label: Osteoma
rejected.why: Osteoma is typically a well-defined, benign tumor, but the presence of a soft-tissue component and cortical destruction suggests a more aggressive process

rejected.label: Eosinophilic Granuloma
rejected.why: Eosinophilic Granuloma often presents with a single, well-defined lytic lesion, but the size and soap-bubble appearance of the lesion in this case are not typical

rejected.label: Ewing's Sarcoma
rejected.why: Ewing's Sarcoma is a highly aggressive tumor, but the lack of significant soft-tissue swelling and the presence of a well-circumscribed mass on examination make it less likely

rejected.label: Brown Tumor
rejected.why: While Brown Tumor is a consideration, the overall clinical and radiographic presentation is more consistent with Giant Cell Tumor
